quoted_text: A digital health application shall retain personally identifiable user-entered wellbeing records for no longer than 24 months after the user's last active session, unless the user has explicitly opted in to longer retention.
candidate_requirement: The app shall retain personally identifiable user-entered wellbeing records for no longer than 24 months after the user's last active session, unless the user has explicitly opted in to longer retention.
rationale: The clause sets a maximum retention period with a single explicit opt-in exception, which the software has to enforce.

quoted_text: Where a user requests deletion of their account, the application shall erase all personally identifiable wellbeing records within 30 days of the request.
candidate_requirement: The app shall erase all personally identifiable wellbeing records within 30 days of a user's request to delete their account.
rationale: The clause states a deletion obligation with an explicit 30-day deadline measured from the user's request.

quoted_text: Aggregate statistics derived from user records may be retained indefinitely provided they cannot be re-identified.
candidate_requirement: The app shall ensure that any aggregate statistics derived from user records that it retains indefinitely cannot be re-identified.
rationale: borderline: the clause is a permission rather than an obligation; only its proviso is testable, so the candidate inverts the permission into its condition. Reviewer must confirm this inversion is a fair reading and not a strengthening.

quoted_text: The application shall enable the user to export their complete wellbeing record in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
candidate_requirement: The app shall enable the user to export their complete wellbeing record in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
rationale: The clause is already a single testable obligation on the software; NOTE 5.2.2 (a rendered PDF does not satisfy it) is the verification criterion, not a separate requirement.

quoted_text: All personally identifiable data transmitted between the application and any remote service shall be protected in transit using a current, non-deprecated transport encryption protocol.
candidate_requirement: The app shall protect all personally identifiable data transmitted between the app and any remote service in transit using a current, non-deprecated transport encryption protocol.
rationale: borderline category: this is strictly a security obligation and is filed under PRIV only because the catalog declares no separate security characteristic (see 00-scope.md Q2); the obligation itself is stated plainly by the clause.

quoted_text: Where an application collects free-text entries from the user, it shall provide the user with a persistently reachable route to crisis support information from any screen on which free-text entry is possible.
candidate_requirement: The app shall provide a persistently reachable route to crisis support information from any screen on which free-text entry is possible.
rationale: The clause makes crisis signposting a per-screen availability obligation wherever free-text entry is offered.

quoted_text: The application shall not present the user with an automated assessment of suicide risk.
candidate_requirement: The app shall not present the user with an automated assessment of suicide risk.
rationale: The clause is an outright prohibition on a software behaviour and is testable by inspection of what the app displays.

quoted_text: The application shall display, on first use, a statement that it is not a substitute for professional care.
candidate_requirement: The app shall display, on first use, a statement that it is not a substitute for professional care.
rationale: The clause obliges a specific disclosure at a specific point in the user journey.

quoted_text: Any therapeutic content presented to the user shall carry an identifiable source and a date of last clinical review.
candidate_requirement: The app shall present an identifiable source with any therapeutic content shown to the user.
rationale: The clause carries two obligations; this candidate covers source attribution only, split per the one-obligation rule (paired with NSAIDH104-010).

quoted_text: Any therapeutic content presented to the user shall carry an identifiable source and a date of last clinical review.
candidate_requirement: The app shall present a date of last clinical review with any therapeutic content shown to the user.
rationale: Second obligation of the same clause, split from NSAIDH104-009 so that each requirement is singular and separately auditable.

quoted_text: Therapeutic content whose last clinical review is more than 36 months old shall be withdrawn or re-reviewed.
candidate_requirement: The app shall not present therapeutic content whose last clinical review is more than 36 months old.
rationale: borderline: the clause offers two remedies (withdraw or re-review) and arguably obliges the publisher rather than the software; the candidate renders the single observable in-product outcome, since re-reviewed content resets its review date. Reviewer must confirm this is not a strengthening and must settle the operator-vs-software scope question.

quoted_text: The application shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
candidate_requirement: The app shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
rationale: The clause is a standards-compliance constraint; it belongs in SRS 3.6 design constraints as well as being the anchor of the accessibility category.

quoted_text: The application shall permit the user to increase text size to at least 200 % of the default without loss of content or functionality.
candidate_requirement: The app shall permit the user to increase text size to at least 200 % of the default without loss of content or functionality.
rationale: The clause gives a measurable threshold and a stated failure condition, so it is directly verifiable.

quoted_text: The application shall permit the user to disable all non-essential notifications, and shall retain that preference across application updates.
candidate_requirement: The app shall permit the user to disable all non-essential notifications.
rationale: First of two obligations in the clause, split per the one-obligation rule (paired with NSAIDH104-015); filed under PERS as user control over how the app addresses them.

quoted_text: The application shall permit the user to disable all non-essential notifications, and shall retain that preference across application updates.
candidate_requirement: The app shall retain the user's notification preference across application updates.
rationale: Second obligation of the same clause; persistence across updates is separately testable from the ability to set the preference.

quoted_text: The application shall not send engagement-driven notifications between 22:00 and 07:00 in the user's local time zone unless the user has explicitly configured otherwise.
candidate_requirement: The app shall not send engagement-driven notifications between 22:00 and 07:00 in the user's local time zone unless the user has explicitly configured otherwise.
rationale: borderline category: also touches PERS through the user-configuration exception, but the clause's default protects the user rather than tailoring the experience, so SAFE is the better fit.

quoted_text: Where the application adapts content on the basis of user data, it shall disclose to the user that adaptation is occurring and on what categories of data it is based.
candidate_requirement: The app shall disclose to the user that content adaptation is occurring, where it adapts content on the basis of user data.
rationale: First of two disclosure obligations in the clause, split per the one-obligation rule (paired with NSAIDH104-018).

quoted_text: Where the application adapts content on the basis of user data, it shall disclose to the user that adaptation is occurring and on what categories of data it is based.
candidate_requirement: The app shall disclose to the user the categories of data on which content adaptation is based, where it adapts content on the basis of user data.
rationale: Second obligation of the same clause; disclosing the data categories is separately testable from disclosing that adaptation happens at all.
